newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman Salalah Port Services in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Oman Salalah Port Services in IPO.

text.p: Oman's newly-formed Salalah Port Services Company (SPS) said it would offer 2.58 million shares at one rial each in an initial public offering.
Subscription would run from June 9 to July 8. The minimum subscription is 100 shares, SPS said in a statement.
The shares on offer account for 20 percent of the company's intended paid-up capital of 12.9 million rials. SPS has an authorised capital of 20 million rials.
It said the founders had underwritten 10.32 million shares.
SPS said founders and shareholders were required to pay 50 percent of the value of their subscription up front. The balance is to paid on request within three years.
SPS is being formed to develop the Gulf state's port of Mina Raysut which Oman hopes will establish it as a gateway for container traffic in the Gulf, east Africa and India.

SPS major founder shareholders are the Omani government with 20 percent, CSX Corp's Sea-Land Services and Denmark's A.P. Moeller shipping group with 15 percent each and Dhofar International Development and Investment with 13 percent. Other founders include local firms and eight pension funds.
